titre: TOS: system calls, supervisor mode and vectors
resume: Your program now lives under TOS, the Atari's system, which it calls with `TRAP` to display text or change a color. As on a real ST, it now starts in **user mode**, which protects the machine: `Supexec` lets it leave that mode for the length of one routine, and `Setexec` lets it install its own exception routines. Module 2 of the Atari ST manual and exercise 2 of its module 7.

atari-ch04-rappel.introduction: Three questions on the previous chapters, without rereading the lessons. Getting it wrong here does not matter: searching is what makes it stick.

q1.enonce: What is D2, the sum computed by the loop?
q1.explication: The counter starts at 4, so DBRA goes round 5 times: 5 × 3 = 15.

q2.enonce: What is D0 at the end?
q2.explication: 15 ÷ 6 = 2, remainder 3: DIVU stores the quotient in the low word and the remainder in the high word.

q3.enonce: At the moment of the final `RTS`, what must be on top of the stack?
choix: The return address left by TOS when the program started
Nothing: the stack must be empty
q3.explication: `RTS` pops the return address; if the program has left something else on top, it jumps anywhere.

atari-ch04-cours-trap.source: Rephrased from the Atari ST manual v1 and v2 (§ 2.2-2.3) and the Féroce Lapin course; functions checked in the simulated TOS

atari-ch04-ex-bonjour.introduction: Watch the stack while the program prepares the call, then the Text output area when the GEMDOS displays the message.

explications.2: `PEA` pushes the address of the text and SP goes down by 4; in user mode, this is the USP stack.
explications.3: The function number, 9 for Cconws, takes 2 more bytes on the stack.
explications.4: `TRAP #1` calls the GEMDOS, which reads the number and the parameter from the stack and displays the text up to its final 0.
explications.5: The program cleans 4 + 2 = 6 bytes off the stack, and SP returns to its starting value.
explications.6: The pushed 0 selects the Pterm0 function.
explications.7: The GEMDOS ends the program and hands control back to the GEM desktop, without returning.

atari-ch04-ex-bonjour.conclusion: Every system call pushes its parameters then its number, executes `TRAP` and cleans up the stack on return.

atari-ch04-pred-cconout.introduction: The program calls Cconout (GEMDOS 2), which displays a single character, twice.

q1.explication: The character is the parameter pushed before the function number: the first call displays 'O', the second 'K'.

choix: Because two words were pushed (2 + 2 bytes)
Because TRAP removes 2 bytes by itself
q2.explication: The character and the number take one word each, that is 4 bytes; with Cconws, the address is a long word, hence 4 + 2 = 6.

atari-ch04-exo-nettoyer.enonce: This program does display `SALUT`, then crashes on the `RTS`. Add the missing line after the `TRAP`.
indices: How many bytes were pushed before the TRAP?

atari-ch04-exo-ordonner.titre: Put the call back in order
atari-ch04-exo-ordonner.enonce: Put the lines back in order to display `A` with Cconout, then end with Pterm0.
indices: The parameter first, then the number, the TRAP and the cleanup.

atari-ch04-exo-afficher.enonce: Display the text `TEXTE`, already defined, with Cconws, then end with Pterm0.

atari-ch04-exo-etoiles.enonce: Display five stars, `*****`, by calling Cconout in a loop, then end with Pterm0.
indices: TOS may modify D0-D2: choose a counter that it preserves.
A counter in D3 and `DBRA`; the body of the loop pushes `'*'`, then 2, calls `TRAP #1` and cleans up 4 bytes.

atari-ch04-cours-superviseur.source: Rephrased from the Atari ST manual v2 (§ 1.4, exercise 7.1-2), the manual v1 (§ 2.3) and the EPITA course (II.2)

atari-ch04-ex-supexec.titre: Changing the background color with Supexec
atari-ch04-ex-supexec.introduction: This is exercise 2 of module 7 of the manual, completed: the routine runs in supervisor mode so that it can touch the palette and a system variable. Watch the S bit and the switch of A7 from the user stack to the supervisor stack.

explications.2: The program pushes the address of the routine to run.
explications.3: Number 38 selects the XBIOS function Supexec.
explications.4: The XBIOS switches to supervisor mode (S = 1, A7 = SSP) and calls ROUTINE, where the PC now is.
explications.9: In supervisor mode, writing to the palette is allowed, and the background turns blue.
explications.10: So is writing to the system variable `conterm` ($484): its bit 0, the key click, drops to 0.
explications.11: The routine's `RTS` returns into the XBIOS, which switches back to user mode (S = 0) and hands control back just after the TRAP.
explications.5: Back in user mode, the program cleans the 6 bytes off the stack.

atari-ch04-ex-supexec.conclusion: Supexec keeps supervisor mode for the only instructions that need it, and the rest of the program keeps the protections of user mode.

atari-ch04-pred-bus.introduction: The program writes to the palette without going through Supexec, so in user mode.

q1.explication: In user mode, the hardware registers ($FF8000 and above) are protected, and the first access causes a bus error (exception 2). Since $FF8240 is even, it is not an address error.

atari-ch04-exo-vert.enonce: This program should turn the background green (`$070`), but it crashes with 2 bombs. Fix it by having the palette written by a routine called with Supexec.
indices: Move the `MOVE.W` into a routine that ends with `RTS`.

atari-ch04-exo-setcolor.titre: Changing a color without supervisor mode
atari-ch04-exo-setcolor.enonce: The XBIOS function 7, `Setcolor(number, color)`, changes a color without you switching to supervisor mode. Set color 0 to yellow (`$770`), then end with Pterm0.
indices: The parameters are pushed from last to first: the color, then the number, then 7.
Three words pushed: 6 bytes to clean up.

atari-ch04-exo-conterm.enonce: Store the byte `conterm` (address `$484`) in D7 without crashing, then end with Pterm0. TOS preserves D7, which therefore keeps its value after the routine.
indices: In user mode, reading $484 causes a bus error: go through Supexec.

atari-ch04-cours-vecteurs.titre: The vector table, RTE and Setexec
atari-ch04-cours-vecteurs.source: Rephrased from the Atari ST manual v1 (§ 2.1) and v2 (§ 2.1), the M68000PRM (chapter 6, exceptions) and the Féroce Lapin course

atari-ch04-ex-setexec.introduction: The program installs a routine on `TRAP #3`, which is free on the Atari, then calls it: watch the switch to supervisor mode at the TRAP and the return to user mode at the `RTE`.

explications.2: The first parameter pushed is the address of the routine.
explications.3: The vector number of TRAP #3 is 32 + 3 = 35.
explications.4: Number 5 selects the BIOS function Setexec.
explications.5: The BIOS writes the address of the routine into vector 35, at address $8C, and returns the old one in D0.
explications.8: On `TRAP #3`, the 68000 switches to supervisor mode, pushes the PC and the SR onto the supervisor stack, reads vector 35 and jumps to MAROUTINE.
explications.12: The routine doubles D0, which is now 40.
explications.13: `RTE` pops the SR, which brings back user mode, then the PC: the program resumes just after the TRAP.

atari-ch04-ex-setexec.conclusion: An exception routine ends with `RTE`, which also restores the status register, and a real program puts the old vector back before quitting.

atari-ch04-pred-pile-trap.introduction: The routine reads what the 68000 pushed during the TRAP; before the call, the flags are all 0 and the interrupt mask is 3.

q1.enonce: What is D6 (the word on top of the supervisor stack)?
q1.explication: The 68000 pushes the PC, then the old SR, which is therefore on top: S at 0 (user mode), mask 3 and flags at 0 give $0300.

q2.enonce: And D5, the long word read at `2(SP)`?
choix: The address of the instruction after TRAP #4
q2.explication: For a TRAP, the pushed PC is that of the next instruction, so that after RTE the program carries on.

atari-ch04-exo-vecteur.enonce: Replace the `0` with the vector number of TRAP #5, so that the routine runs and sets D0 to 7.

atari-ch04-exo-divzero.enonce: This program divides by zero and displays 5 bombs. At the start, use Setexec to install on vector 5 a routine that sets D7 to −1 and returns with `RTE`, so that the program gets as far as Pterm0.

atari-ch04-exo-compteur.enonce: Install on TRAP #4 a routine that adds 1 to D6. The program calls it three times, and D6 must be 3 at the end.

atari-ch04-bonus-palette.enonce: The XBIOS function 6, Setpalette, installs all 16 colors at once from a table of 16 words. Install the palette `PALETTE`, a gradient from black to red then to white by way of orange, and end with Pterm0.
indices: A single parameter: the address of the table (`PEA PALETTE`).

q1.explication: TRAP #1 calls the GEMDOS, #13 the BIOS and #14 the XBIOS.

q2.enonce: After `PEA TEXTE` / `MOVE.W #9,-(SP)` / `TRAP #1`, by how much must SP be corrected?
q2.explication: A 4-byte address and a 2-byte function number.

q3.enonce: In which register does TOS return the result of a function?
q3.explication: TOS always returns its value in D0.

q10.enonce: A `MOVE.W` to an odd address causes…
q10.explication: A word must be stored at an even address, otherwise the 68000 raises exception 3, the address error.

q4.enonce: Which registers may TOS modify during a call?
q4.explication: D0-D2 and A0-A2 are scratch registers; D3-D7 and A3-A6 are preserved.

q5.enonce: A program in user mode writes to `$FF8240`. What happens?
q5.explication: In user mode, the hardware registers are protected and the access causes a bus error.

choix: Running a routine in supervisor mode
q6.explication: The routine runs in supervisor mode, then the program returns to user mode.

q11.enonce: A subroutine starts with `MOVEM.L D3/A3,-(SP)`. By how much has SP gone down?
q11.explication: Two registers saved in `.L`, that is 2 × 4 = 8 bytes.

q7.enonce: At what address is the vector of TRAP #1?

q8.enonce: How does an exception routine end?
q8.explication: `RTE` pops the SR and the PC that the exception pushed.

q9.enonce: What does Setexec return in D0?
q9.explication: Setexec returns the old address, to be put back before quitting.
